metadata.technology: Capacitive Soil Moisture Sensor Probe (with MCU + radio)
metadata.technology_specification: Capacitive soil moisture sensor probe with integrated microcontroller unit (MCU) and wireless radio module
metadata.technology_reasoning: Capacitive soil moisture sensors are the industry standard for low-cost, reliable soil moisture measurement due to their resistance to corrosion compared to resistive sensors. The integration of an MCU and wireless radio, typically sub-GHz or BLE modules, is standard in modern smart sensor probes for remote monitoring and data transmission in agriculture and environmental sensing.

components.reasoning: This is the core sensing element, typically a printed PCB or coated probe that measures soil permittivity changes. It is always present and sourced separately as a distinct sensor unit.
The MCU is the central control and data processing unit, essential for sensor data acquisition and processing; it is a standard discrete electronic component.

components.component: Wireless Radio Module (e.g., Sub-GHz or BLE)
components.reasoning: Wireless communication modules are typically integrated as separate subassemblies to enable remote data transmission; this component is nearly universal in connected soil moisture probes.
The PCB physically supports and electrically connects the sensor, MCU, and radio modules; it is an essential, separately manufactured structural electronic platform.
Power source for the probe, often a replaceable or rechargeable lithium coin cell or battery pack, typically procured separately.
Protects internal electronics from environmental factors like moisture and soil ingress; usually a molded plastic or epoxy housing sourced as a distinct structural component.
Wireless radios require an antenna component (either PCB trace or discrete antenna) which is often a separate component or subassembly critical for communication.
